question: Should OpenClaw sponsor Iroh as a core experimental Gateway transport, and if so should the first accepted contract use native Gateway framing or a narrower localhost bridge?
rationale: Current main has no Iroh transport, while the RFC intentionally leaves core networking, identity, configuration, and supported-client decisions unresolved.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed native transport
options.body: Accept native Gateway framing over Iroh streams with endpoint identity enforcement and a minimal explicit configuration surface.

options.title: Start with a localhost bridge
options.body: Prototype Iroh connectivity behind the existing local WebSocket server and defer a new native framing contract.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep remote access on existing WebSocket, Tailscale, SSH, TLS, and operator-managed network paths.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed native transport
recommendation.body: Accept native Gateway framing over Iroh streams with endpoint identity enforcement and a minimal explicit configuration surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal covers Gateway authentication, pairing, token scopes, and protocol boundaries central to this decision.
